messages:
ani: Noticing a weird pattern in us-east:dedicated-pool-2 this morning. GPU utilization steady but a bunch of hosts suddenly started dropping connections to our control-plane and spawned retries -> tail latency spikes for tenants in that pool.

will: any network errors in dmesg or driver logs?

ani: yes, saw a flurry of NAT port exhaustion counters on the edge NATs. sockets were hitting ephemeral port limits and we saw RSTs back to the clients.

sam: tenant Y's rollout? they started a fanout of short-lived health checks to the control plane at 06:02. lots of new TCP 4-tuples -> ephemeral ports burned.

mira: pulled S-NAT metrics: ephemeral_port_count peaked at 64k for a single nat-instance and timeouts followed. We also saw a spike in TCP_RETRIES and connection_reuse=low.

ops-bot: alert: nat-instance-7 ephemeral_port_exhaustion (count=65535) 2025-09-04T06:04:12Z.

will: root cause looks like massive 1-2s connections from tens of thousands of short-lived clients (health checks / preconnects). NAT mapping table thrashed and driver started dropping.

ani: quick mitigation I propose: 1) scale out SNAT pool (add 2 instances), 2) apply per-tenant ephemeral-port caps via egress-proxy (soft limit), 3) temporarily reduce tenant Y health-check fanout to 5%.

sam: agree. Also we should enable long-lived connection pooling at the agent side asap to reduce 4-tuple churn. Patch ready to flip on for canary.

mira: adding route-level mitigation: divert egress from dedicated-pool-2 to nat-instance-9/10 which have spare capacity. Will update routing table.

net-bot: routing change applied: us-east/dedicated-pool-2 -> nat-9,nat-10 (id: route-evade-20250904).

ani: applying soft tenant override on Y: `curl -XPOST https://ops-api/overrides -d '{"tenant":"Y","healthcheck_fanout":2,"ttl":"1h"}'`

ops-bot: override accepted (id: ov-992a).

mira: after routing shift and SNAT scale, ephemeral_port_count back to 10k and connection reuse improved. tail latency dropped from 220ms 95p -> 48ms in 7 minutes.

will: follow-ups: 1) infra: add ephemeral port accounting per-tenant + quota enforcement (we need visibility before soft caps), 2) platform: require connection pooling and backoff for health-check libraries, 3) networking: add auto-scale trigger for nat-instances when port usage crosses 70%.

sam: I'll open PR for client-side pooling with a feature flag for canaries. will include a stress test that simulates 50k concurrent short connections.

ani: cost note: adding 2 nat instances ~ $0.5/hr; implementing autoscale is dev + 1 day. Per-tenant quotas likely modest infra cost.

mira: long term we should avoid funneling all egress through a small set of NATs for a pool. Proposal: per-pool distributed SNAT and route-aware egress so a pool doesn't take down a single nat.

ops-bot: incident tag `ephemeral-port-threshold` created. escalate if recurs after 24h.

will: excellent. keeping this thread open until we validate canary with pooled connections for 2 hours. ping here after 30m with metrics.

ani: 15m in: metrics look stable. closing aggressive overrides at 07:20 but keeping autoscale ticket open.

net-bot: note: logged NAT telemetry snapshot to /telemetry/nat/20250904-06:00-07:00 for postmortem.
